facts.fact: The government's communiqué of 22 April 2026 states that the computerised national civil-status register, developed and made operational under loi n°2019-29 of 1 July 2019, is operational in 102 communes of Niger and that efforts continue to computerise the other communes; it gives no total of communes.
facts.system: registre national de l'état civil informatisé

facts.fact: The communiqué of 22 April 2026 describes a computerised national civil-status register operational in communes, from which civil-status acts are printed on secured paper ('à partir du système informatisé'); it does not say whether communes enter online or by synchronising.
facts.system: registre national de l'état civil informatisé

facts.fact: The civil-status ordonnance was adopted on 22 April 2026 under the heading of the Ministère de l'Intérieur, de la Sécurité Publique et de l'Administration du Territoire, which also has oversight of the ANEI created the same day; the communiqué presents the computerised register as a result of the state's 2019 reform.
facts.system: registre national de l'état civil informatisé

facts.fact: On 22 April 2026 the Council of Ministers adopted the ordonnance on the civil-status regime, correcting the 2019 law to cover the constitution and use of the national civil-status register, electronic issue and electronic signature of civil-status acts, the A4 secured paper for acts printed from the computerised system, and computerised civil status at the foreign ministry's central service.
facts.system: registre national de l'état civil informatisé
